claims.text: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow.
Russian President Vladimir Putin told US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner during their meeting in Moscow that the current situation is not so easy.
Steve Witkoff thanked Vladimir Putin for agreeing with Ukraine to halt strikes on each other's capitals for three days.
US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are scheduled to travel to Kyiv on Sunday for diplomatic engagements.
US President Donald Trump stated on Friday that Witkoff and Kushner were bringing a proposal to end the war.
Talks between Vladimir Putin and the US envoys at the Kremlin lasted for three hours, according to Russian state media.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Ukraine is ready to refrain from strikes on Moscow through the end of Saturday, as well as on Sunday and Monday.
Vladimir Putin ordered a halt to strikes on Kyiv for three days due to the visit by US envoys.
Vladimir Putin stated in televised remarks that Russia had not agreed to a ceasefire for areas of Ukraine outside of Kyiv.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia fired demonstrative strikes on airports in Kyiv and Boryspil overnight prior to his planned meeting with US envoys.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said an overnight Russian strike on a civilian building in the Dnipro region killed four people and injured five others.
CIA Director John Ratcliffe paid a rare visit to the Russian capital a little over a week prior to Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner's visit.
US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin on Saturday.
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov stated that Vladimir Putin gave the order from midnight Saturday not to strike Kyiv for three days.
Russian strikes on Saturday killed at least seven people in Ukraine, including two in the Bucha district outside Kyiv.
Oleksandr Hanzha, head of the local military administration, stated that an overnight Russian strike at a factory in the Dnipropetrovsk region killed five people and wounded five others.
A Russian drone hit the headquarters of Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) on Friday.
Ground troops in Ukraine remain locked along a 775-mile frontline.
Vladimir Putin stated at the start of the meeting in Moscow that it is convenient for Russia to work with Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.
Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner were received in Moscow by Kirill Dmitriev, Vladimir Putin's investment envoy.
US Central Command stated it permanently disabled two Iran-linked oil tankers and completely destroyed a third in the Gulf of Oman.
US Central Command stated the strikes on Iranian tankers were in retaliation for Tehran targeting a US aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer.
Kharg Island hosts Iran's main oil export terminal, handling approximately 90% of the country's crude oil exports via pipes from the mainland.
Iranian state media Irib reported that Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps retaliated against six ships, including three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and three US-affiliated vessels.
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth posted on social media that if Iran shoots at US ships, the US will destroy and sink their oil tankers.
The US resumed attacks against Iran after striking two rocket launchers to prevent them from laying naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz.
The average price for a gallon of diesel in the US reached $5.85, up from $3.71 a year prior.
US Vice President JD Vance stated he was extremely sceptical regarding Iranian claims that US strikes killed four people at a wedding in Sirik, Iran.
US Central Command reported that its forces struck three Iranian crude oil carriers on Saturday.
US Central Command commander Admiral Brad Cooper stated that the US military would destroy Iran's oil fleet if necessary to defend American forces.

A preliminary US military inquiry found that a February 28 strike on a school compound in Minab that killed at least 156 people resulted from outdated coordinates identifying the school as part of a naval base.
US Central Command identified the permanently disabled tankers as M/T Downy, struck off Kharg Island, and M/T Stark 1, struck near Jask.
US Central Command identified the destroyed third tanker as M/T Kylo, also known as Noxen, which was struck in the Gulf of Oman.
Chandika Kumari Shrestha, 64, was rescued semi-conscious from the upper floor of a four-storey house buried in debris in Betrawati, Nuwakot district, 10 days after floods hit Nepal.
Chinese worker Luhaitao was rescued alive from 225 metres inside the Audit 4 tunnel of the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project in Rasuwa.
Luhaitao was rescued by a joint team of Nepal army personnel and South Korean experts and flown to Birendra Military Hospital.
Local officials in Betrawati stated that only five of around 300 houses remained standing after the flood.
More than 1,300 people were killed after a collapse of ice, rock, and mud swept through a Himalayan valley in Nepal.
Nepal's national disaster authority reported that the flood disaster killed at least 1,331 people in Nepal and left about 5,000 missing, including 589 foreign nationals.
Officials in Tibet recorded 31 deaths and 531 people missing following the disaster across the border.
About 900 workers remain unaccounted for at hydropower construction sites in Nepal, with roughly 500 believed trapped inside tunnels across 12 projects.
Nearly 100% of Nepal's electricity comes from hydropower, earning nearly $200m annually from exports to India and Bangladesh.
The floods severely damaged 12 hydropower plants in the Trishuli River basin and knocked out more than 10% of Nepal's total power generation capacity.
The Upper Trishuli-1 project is valued at about $647m and represents one of Nepal's largest foreign direct investment ventures.
Nepal's disaster management agency reported that at least 1,375 people have been killed in the floods, with more than 5,000 missing.
The United Nations voted on Friday to support a shift away from the 16th-century Mercator global map toward one reflecting countries' true sizes.
The UN General Assembly adopted the Correct the Map resolution to address discrepancies in the Mercator map projection.
The African continent is approximately 14 times larger than Greenland in reality, despite appearing similar in size on the Mercator map.
Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator created the Mercator map in 1569 to aid European sailors in ocean navigation.
The Equal Earth map projection was developed by a team of cartographers in 2018 and was adopted by African Union members in February.
The African-led UN resolution championing equal-area map projections was adopted with 164 countries voting in favour, one voting against, and six abstaining.
India voted in favour of the UN map resolution, while the United States was the only country to vote against it.
Ukraine abstained from the UN vote over concerns regarding how certain Equal Earth maps depict Ukrainian territories occupied by Russia.
Togo's Foreign Minister Robert Dussey stated that a fair map does not change world geography but changes how the world is seen.
The US delegation objected to the UN map resolution, claiming it was part of a larger radical ideological project.
Togo introduced the Correct the Map resolution at the UN on behalf of the 54 African member states and supported by the African Union.
Yaryna Ferencevych, deputy US representative to the UN Economic and Social Council, stated that resolutions like Correct the Map are causing the institution to lose credibility.
